en: The Apadāna of the Elder Subhadda Upāli-vagga, Number 9 In the past, when the Buddha Kassapa was the World-Honored One, I was a monk named Subhadda, dwelling in the forest. At that time, I saw the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, And having seen him, I paid homage with my head at his feet. Having bowed my head to the feet of the Great Sage, I sat down to one side and spoke these words: "O Blessed One, please grant me the going-forth; May I receive ordination in the Dhamma and Vinaya. The Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, spoke these words to me: "Come, monk," he said, and that very moment I became a monk. Having gone forth under the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, I practiced the holy life with diligence and vigor. For eighty-four thousand years I lived as a forest-dweller, And during that time I never once felt sloth or torpor. When I had completed that holy life, I passed away from that human existence. By virtue of that wholesome deed, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. There I enjoyed divine pleasures for a long time, And after passing away from there, I was reborn among humans. Seven times I was born in the human world, And seven times I attained the state of a Wheel-Turning Monarch. Now, having been born in this final existence, I have reached the end of suffering and am free from all bonds. I have attained the supreme fruit of Arhatship, And I dwell in peace, cooled and without fever. This is my last birth; there will be no further becoming. Having cut off the stream of existence, I have transcended all suffering. Thus did I speak these verses of praise, And by that merit I attained the state of an Arhat.

I have fulfilled the training and accomplished what was to be done; I have laid down the heavy burden and am liberated through right knowledge. I pay homage to the Buddha, the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One, Who has crossed over the flood and reached the further shore. I pay homage to the Dhamma, the well-expounded teaching, Which leads to Nirvana and is lived out by those who are truly wise. I pay homage to the Sangha, the assembly of the noble ones, The supreme field of merit for the world of gods and men. I have paid homage to the Triple Gem, And by that merit I have attained the state of an Arhat. I have reached the goal of the holy life, And I dwell in peace, cooled and without fever. “Padumuttara, the Knower of the World,
the recipient of offerings,
having uplifted the people, ”
The one of great renown attains Nibbāna.
And as the Perfectly Awakened One passes into Nibbāna,
the ten-thousandfold world system trembles.
A great multitude of people was there,
and the gods gathered at that time;
having filled [the vessel] with sandalwood, they offered it.
And with *tagara* and jasmine flowers,
joyful with a joyful heart,
I offered them to the Supreme among Men.
Knowing my intention,
the Teacher, the unsurpassed one in the world,
remained lying down even as he was the Fully Awakened One.
He spoke these verses:
“He who covered me with a garland of fragrant flowers at the time of my final passing;”
I shall proclaim that;
listen to me as I speak.
Having passed away from here, this person—
He will go to the Tusita realm;
having exercised sovereignty there,
he will proceed to the Nimmānarati heaven.
By this very means,
having offered that most excellent garland, he,
delighted by his own deed, [proceeded].
He will experience prosperity.
Furthermore, this person will be reborn in the Tusita realm.
Having passed away from that body,
he will go to the human state;
he is the Sakyan son, the Great Naga.
Foremost in the world including the devas;
having awakened many beings,
the Visionary One will pass into Nibbāna.
Then, having approached and being impelled by the root of his own wholesome merit,
he drew near to the Fully Awakened One.
When he asks a question,
then the All-Knowing One, the Perfectly Awakened One, the Leader of the World, will cause him to laugh.
Having fully understood meritorious action,
he will reveal the truths;
and this question has been undertaken.
Contented and with a one-pointed mind,
having paid homage to the Teacher,
he will request the going forth.
Seeing his mind full of serene confidence,
satisfied by his own karma,
that Buddha will grant him the going forth.
Skilled in the supreme path,
this person, having exerted effort in the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One;
"Having fully understood all taints,
he will attain Nibbāna, free from taints.
The fifth recitation section.
Bound by former karma,
one-pointed and well-composed,
he is the true-born son of the Buddha.
I am well-fashioned by the Dhamma.
Having approached the King of Dhamma,
I asked the supreme question.
And as he spoke this question to me,
he led me toward the stream of Dhamma.
Having understood his Dhamma, I—
I dwelt delighted in the Teaching;
having fully understood all taints,
I live free from taints.
One hundred thousand aeons ago,
the Leader, supreme among those born from the lotus,
attained Parinirvāṇa, free from all clinging.
Like a lamp when its oil is exhausted,
the stupa made of jewels was seven yojanas in height.
There I honored a banner,
auspicious in every way and delightful,
belonging to the Buddha Kassapa.
Tissa was a noble disciple;
he was my own biological son,
an heir to the Conqueror’s teaching.
With an inferior mind,
I spoke unwholesome words;
by the ripening of that kamma,
Afterwards, there was bliss for me:
in the Sal grove at Upavattana,
on my final couch, the Sage [passed away].
The Great Hero, the Beneficent,
Compassionate Victor, ordained him;
indeed, ordination takes place this very day.
Today is the full ordination;
today is the final Nibbāna,
in the presence of the Supreme among Bipeds.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Subhadda speak these verses.
This is the ninth legend of the elder Subhadda.
